## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `subscriber-weighted-salience`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-08-09T20:05:21.715Z.

Context relevance ledger (35): subscriber-weighted item salience — an item is more relevant to an agent's working set the more declared predicates read it, because a change there propagates into enforcement instead of staying local, and the propagation is knowable from the record rather than guessed from the prose.

Recorded 2026-08-09 evening, from the remote-effect measurement on pm-n7rr and horizon AK. The measurement showed that a mutating verb's real blast radius is not the files it writes but the set of external predicates over the record whose value it changes. Entry (34) established that the relevance of a fact decays with the lifetime of the property it describes rather than the lifetime of its owner. This entry is the retrieval-side consequence of the same observation applied to items rather than facts: an item that several declared predicates depend upon is load-bearing in a way no metadata field currently expresses, and an assembler that ranks it identically to an item nothing reads is discarding information the record already contains.

The signal. For each item, the count and kind of declared predicates whose evaluation reads it, weighted by the disposition of each predicate — an enforcing bound outranks a held one, and a held one outranks a retired one. The value is a boost applied to items already admitted by the retrieval stage, never an admission criterion of its own, because a subscriber count says how consequential a change would be and says nothing about whether the item answers the question being asked.

Degeneracy clauses, mandatory as for every entry in this ledger. Identically uniform when the predicate registry is empty, which is the state today and will remain the state until horizon AK's registry exists, so the entry costs nothing before it can be computed. Identically uniform on a corpus where every item has the same subscriber count. Never raises a declared ceiling and never admits an item the retrieval stage rejected. Bounded by construction: the registry is repository data of registry size, not corpus size, so the computation is independent of item count and remains valid at a million items where a graph-centrality proxy for the same intuition would not.

Why it is not simply centrality, which is the objection this entry has to answer. Graph centrality measures how connected an item is to other items, and the typed graph is authored deliberately, so centrality partly measures how much attention an item has already received. Subscriber weight measures something the graph cannot see at all: coupling to mechanisms that live outside the record and are not nodes in it. The two are expected to correlate weakly and to disagree in the interesting cases, and the disagreement is the diagnostic — an item with high subscriber weight and low centrality is a silent coupling, which is precisely the failure horizon AK names.

Candidate only, routed through pm-g8t7b9 like every other entry in this ledger, and explicitly not weighted on the single incident that motivated it. It is blocked in practice by the registry it reads, and it should not be implemented before there is a registry with more than a handful of rows, because a signal fitted to three subscribers would encode this session's accidents as a prior.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
